name: Handle customer, dealer and broker service requests (equipment finance company)
summary: Customer service representatives answer about 11,000 calls and e-mails a month from lessees, dealers and brokers about existing contracts: balances and payment dates, copies of invoices and contracts, address and banking changes, insurance, disputed charges and payout requests. They verify the caller, look up the contract, settle simple requests on the spot and route payouts, restructures, assumptions, casualty losses and complaints to other teams. Work is uneven because calls peak after billing and debit dates, and about three contacts in ten are not resolved first time, often because the answer depends on another team or because a banking change needs signed documents.

baseline.org_archetype: A privately owned Canadian independent lessor with about 55,000 active contracts and a 24-person customer service team using contact centre telephony, shared mailboxes, the lease management system and document imaging.
baseline.notes: One case is one contact. Repeat contacts about the same issue count as new contacts in the volume and appear here as a rework edge.

trigger: A customer, dealer or broker calls, e-mails, faxes or sends a portal message about an existing contract.
end_state: The request is answered or completed on the contact, confirmed in writing, routed to the team that owns it, or declined because the requester could not be verified.

volume.seasonality: Daily peaks after billing and debit dates (1st and 15th) and Mondays; the high end reflects spring 2020, when lessors took large volumes of COVID-related calls and deferral requests.

evidence.note: Volume from the organisation file (about 0.2 contacts per active contract a month). CFLA's March 2020 survey found 40% of members handling more than 100 COVID-related calls a day.

Cost from the organisation file: Job Bank 2023-2024 Ontario wage for financial customer service representatives (median $22.00) at about 90% for 2019-2022, loaded by 1.35. Twenty representatives also support insurance tracking, collections transfers and outbound work, so about 14.5 FTE on inbound service is an author estimate.
Organisation file cost (loading 1.35). Two supervisors; escalations, approvals and complaint calls; author estimate.

roles.title: Quality and training specialist, customer service

evidence.note: Organisation file cost (loading 1.35). Quality reviews of about 2% of contacts; the rest of the role is training. Author estimate.
Organisation file cost (loading 1.35). Approvals above supervisor limits only; staffing and reporting work is not modelled as steps. Author estimate.

systems.name: Contact centre telephony and shared mailboxes
Lease management system (contracts, schedules, billing, tax codes, asset records, servicing)
Document imaging and contract file store

steps.name: Route the contact to a queue
steps.description: A customer, dealer or broker calls the service line or writes to the shared service mailbox. The phone system plays the menu and routes the call by caller type and topic to the customer service queue; e-mails, faxes and portal messages land in the shared mailbox for the next free representative.
inputs: incoming call, e-mail, fax or portal message

error.defect_description: None introduced; callers sometimes pick the wrong menu option.

evidence.note: Channel split of about 78% phone and 22% written is an author estimate for small business lessees, dealers and brokers in 2019-2022; ContactBabel finds e-mail and web chat take 11.7% of agent time against 58.6% for talk time.

steps.name: Answer the call and take the reason
steps.description: When the call reaches the front of the queue a customer service representative answers, gets the caller's name, company and contract number and the reason for the call.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: ContactBabel reports a mean average speed to answer of 75 seconds in US contact centres in late 2020. The queue time range here is an author estimate, longer on billing-day peaks.

steps.name: Pick up the written request
steps.description: A representative assigned to the mailbox opens the next e-mail, fax or portal message, reads the request and any attachment and finds the contract number.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Mailbox service target of about one business day is an author estimate; written requests wait longer in peaks.

steps.name: Verify identity and authority
steps.description: The representative finds the contract and checks the requester against it: for a customer, questions such as contract number, business address, signer name and last payment amount; for a dealer or broker, that they are the originating partner and may receive only limited information. Requests from unverified callers are declined until a signer authorises them in writing.

error.defect_description: An impostor or an unauthorised third party passes weak verification.

control.basis: PIPEDA Schedule 1, Principle 4.7 (safeguards) and 4.3 (consent): authenticate the requester before disclosing or changing account information; the questions used are set by company policy

next.condition: cannot verify, asked for written authorisation

evidence.note: The OPC safeguards bulletin says organisations must have safeguards and follow proper client authentication procedures. Failure rate and times are author estimates.

steps.name: Look up contract, billing and payment history
steps.description: The representative opens the contract in the lease system (schedule, balance, last payments, returned debits, insurance status, notes from earlier contacts) and the signed documents in imaging.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Classify the request and decide who handles it
steps.description: The representative decides whether the request can be settled on the contact or must go to another team, using the service procedures: questions and copies are handled now, payouts, restructures, assumptions, casualty losses and complaints are routed, and credits above the representative's limit need a supervisor.

error.defect_description: Request routed to the wrong team or handled when it should have been escalated.

next.condition: balance, payment date, invoice or tax question
copy of invoice, contract, schedule or tax letter
one-time payment by debit or fee waiver request
restructure, deferral, assumption or casualty loss
belongs to collections, funding or another team

evidence.note: Request types follow the organisation file and lessor help pages (payments, invoices, tax, banking changes). The mix is an author estimate; in 2020 CFLA found 40% of members handling more than 100 COVID-related calls a day, mostly deferral requests.

steps.name: Answer the account question
steps.description: The representative explains the balance, the next payment date and amount, why an amount changed (tax, insurance charge, late charge) or where a payment was applied, using the payment history on screen.

error.defect_description: Wrong or incomplete answer that leads to a repeat contact.

evidence.note: SQM reports first-call resolution of 71% for billing calls and 73% for account maintenance; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Send the requested document
steps.description: The representative finds the invoice, contract, payment schedule, tax letter or paid-in-full letter in the lease system or imaging, checks it goes only to a party on the contract, and e-mails or faxes it.

error.defect_description: Document for the wrong contract or sent to an unauthorised address.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Update details or start a banking change
steps.description: The representative updates an address, phone or invoice e-mail on the call. For a change of bank account the representative explains that a signed debit agreement and a void cheque from the new account are needed and sends the form.

error.defect_description: Address keyed wrongly so invoices and notices go astray.

evidence.note: National Bank asks for a void cheque from the new account; Rule H1 s.15 requires a payor's PAD agreement for each debit. Split is an author estimate.

steps.name: Wait for the signed debit form and void cheque
steps.description: The customer signs the debit agreement and sends it back with a void cheque by e-mail or fax; some never do and stay on their old account or switch to cheque.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Verify and key the banking change
steps.description: A representative compares the account holder name on the void cheque and the signature with the contract, calls the customer back on the number on file to confirm the change, keys the new account in the lease system before the next debit cut-off, and a second representative checks the keying.

error.defect_description: Account digits keyed wrongly, leading to a rejected debit.

control.basis: Payments Canada Rule H1 s.15 (each debit supported by a payor's PAD agreement for that account) plus internal payment-fraud policy (call-back to the number on file and second-person check)

evidence.note: Agreement requirement from Rule H1; void cheque practice from National Bank. Call-back and second check are common fraud controls; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Investigate a disputed charge
steps.description: The representative reviews the invoice and billing history for the disputed late charge, returned payment fee, tax, insurance charge or amount, and either explains it or decides an adjustment is due under the service guidelines.

error.defect_description: Valid dispute rejected or an unwarranted credit promised.

evidence.note: SQM puts billing-call first-call resolution at 71%. Split is an author estimate.

steps.name: Raise a billing adjustment or one-time debit
steps.description: The representative fills in a billing adjustment request in the lease system work queue (credit, fee waiver, rebill, tax exemption with the certificate attached) or records the customer's authorisation for a one-time debit, with the reason code and support.

error.defect_description: Wrong amount or contract on the request.

control.basis: Delegation of authority (representative credit limit) and Payments Canada Rule H1 s.15(a)(iii): a sporadic or one-time debit needs the payor's authorisation each time

evidence.note: Authorisation rule for sporadic debits from Rule H1; limits and split are author estimates.

steps.name: Handle an insurance question
steps.description: The representative explains the insurance the contract requires or why a protection program charge appeared, takes the customer's certificate of insurance by e-mail and forwards it to insurance tracking.

error.defect_description: Certificate forwarded without the contract number and filed late.

evidence.note: Organisation file process track-equipment-insurance receives certificates from this process. Author estimate.

steps.name: Log a payout or purchase request
steps.description: The representative confirms the contracts, the payout date wanted and the reason (sale of equipment, trade-up through a dealer, purchase option), creates the payout request for lease administration, tells the requester when the quote will arrive and notes the contact.
outputs: payout request in lease administration queue

error.defect_description: Wrong contract or payout date on the request, so the quote must be redone.

evidence.note: National Bank describes lease-end options (purchase at fair market value or the stated option, renew, return, trade up) handled through customer service; quotes come from the organisation file's buyout process. Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Route a restructure, assumption or casualty request
steps.description: The representative takes the basic facts (reason for a deferral, buyer of the business, date and cause of a loss), sends the application or claim form, and creates a task for lease administration with the notes.

error.defect_description: Facts missing from the task so lease administration has to call the customer again.

evidence.note: CFLA describes the surge of deferral requests in 2020; routing targets are from the organisation file. Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Log a complaint
steps.description: When the requester expresses dissatisfaction that needs a recorded response, the representative records it in the complaint log with the facts, the outcome wanted and the contract, acknowledges it and passes it to the supervisor.

error.defect_description: Complaint not logged, so it is missing from compliance reporting.

control.basis: Complaint handling policy: every complaint recorded and reported to compliance

evidence.note: SQM puts complaint-call first-call resolution at 47%, the lowest of any call type. Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Supervisor handles escalation or approval
steps.description: A customer service supervisor reviews the account and the representative's notes, approves or declines a credit or waiver above the representative's limit, or calls the upset customer back.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Delegation of authority: credits and waivers above the representative's limit approved by a supervisor

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Log an IT ticket for an access problem
steps.description: For a customer who cannot log in to the portal or receive e-invoices, the representative checks the e-mail on file, resets access if the procedure allows, or logs an IT ticket with the details.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Transfer to the right team
steps.description: For a customer in arrears who wants to arrange payment, or a dealer asking about funding or commission, the representative warm-transfers the call to collections, funding or the vendor desk and notes the transfer.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Record notes and close the contact
steps.description: The representative types the contact notes and a disposition code in the lease system, sets a follow-up task where something is outstanding and ends the after-call work.

error.defect_description: Notes too thin for the next representative, causing a repeat explanation.

next.condition: needs research or another team's answer

evidence.note: ContactBabel: post-call wrap-up is 9.4% of agent time; SQM: 71% average first-call resolution, so about 29% of callers contact again. Part of that is modelled as callbacks (s24) and part as repeat contacts; split is an author estimate.

steps.name: Send written confirmation
steps.description: Right after the contact the representative e-mails a confirmation of the change, the answer or the next steps, using a template from the service library.

error.defect_description: Confirmation sent to the wrong address.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Quality review of the contact
steps.description: The quality and training specialist listens to the recorded call or reads the e-mail thread, scores it against the scorecard (verification done, accuracy, notes, tone) and gives feedback to the representative.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: A Call Centre Helper poll found 60% of centres monitor 2 to 6 calls per agent a month; 2% of contacts here is about 11 per representative a month. Review happens after the contact is closed.

steps.name: Research and call back
steps.description: For a request that needs another team's answer (billing, lease administration, funding), the representative sends the question, waits for the reply and calls or e-mails the requester back.

error.defect_description: Callback missed, leading to a repeat contact or complaint.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Supervisor resolves the complaint
steps.description: The supervisor reviews the complaint log entry and the account, calls the customer, agrees a resolution and records the outcome and response date in the log for compliance reporting.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Complaint handling policy: supervisor response and log entry within the policy deadline

evidence.note: Organisation file sends complaints to handle-complaints-and-compliance-monitoring. Author estimate.

steps.name: Manager approves a large goodwill credit
steps.description: The manager of customer service reviews a credit or waiver above the supervisor's limit, checks it against the account history and approves or declines it.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Delegation of authority: credits above the supervisor limit approved by the manager

evidence.note: Author estimate.

exceptions.name: Caller cannot be verified
exceptions.description: The caller cannot answer the verification questions or is not a party to the contract; nothing is disclosed until a signer authorises it in writing.

exceptions.name: Banking change waiting for documents
exceptions.description: A new bank account needs a signed debit agreement and void cheque, a call-back and a second check before the next debit; some customers never return the form.

exceptions.name: Credit above the representative's limit
exceptions.description: Disputed charges and waivers above the limit go to a supervisor and occasionally the manager.

exceptions.name: Complaint
exceptions.description: The complaint is logged, the supervisor calls the customer and the outcome goes to compliance reporting.

exceptions.name: Not resolved first time
exceptions.description: The answer depends on another team, so the representative calls back later, or the requester contacts the company again.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from contact to resolution, routing or written confirmation
benchmarks.population: Inbound service contacts at a mid-size lessor (derived)

evidence.note: Derived: about 75 seconds to answer (ContactBabel) plus a handle time of 589 seconds including wrap-up (SQM) gives about 12 minutes for a call resolved first time, the most common case. With written confirmations, banking changes, written requests and callbacks in the mix, the median contact is taken as about 20 minutes. p90 reflects e-mails answered within one to two business days and callbacks; author estimate.

benchmarks.unit: share of callers who do not need to contact again (post-call survey)
benchmarks.population: Over 500 North American call centres benchmarked by SQM Group (2022 report)

benchmarks.unit: seconds of talk and wrap-up time
benchmarks.population: Call centres in SQM Group's FCR benchmark (2022 report)

evidence.note: ContactBabel also reports call abandonment highest in the finance sector.

benchmarks.value: 40% of CFLA respondents had more than 100 COVID-related calls a day

pain_points.description: About three contacts in ten are not resolved first time; many need an answer from billing, lease administration or funding, so customers call again.

evidence.note: Industry FCR of 71%; the dependency on other teams is author judgement.

pain_points.description: Banking changes need a signed form, a void cheque, a call-back and a second check before the debit cut-off; missed cut-offs cause returned debits.

evidence.note: Requirements from the sources; consequence is author judgement.

pain_points.description: Calls peak after billing and debit dates and spiked in 2020 with deferral requests, lengthening queues and abandonment.

evidence.note: COVID call volumes from CFLA; finance-sector abandonment from ContactBabel.

pain_points.description: Verification relies on knowledge questions about the contract, which slows every call and still lets some impostors through.

evidence.note: OPC cases of weak authentication are cited in the bulletin.

sources.title: Call center industry 2022 FCR benchmark results (What is a good FCR rate?)
sources.supports: Average FCR 71% across industries (range 40% to 91%); FCR by call type: general inquiries 74%, account maintenance 73%, billing 71%, complaints 47%; AHT (talk and wrap-up) 589 seconds; financial industries in the moderate band.

sources.title: The US Contact Center HR and Operational Benchmarking Report 2021 (summary)
sources.supports: 214 US contact centres interviewed in Q4 2020: mean average speed to answer 75 seconds; mean service call over six minutes; post-call wrap-up 9.4% and talk 58.6% of agent time; call abandonment highest in the finance sector.

sources.title: Wages for financial customer service representatives (NOC 64400)
sources.supports: Hourly wages 2023-2024: Ontario low $17.95, median $22.00, high $30.39; Toronto region median $22.50.

sources.title: Interpretation bulletin: safeguards
sources.publisher: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada
sources.supports: Principle 4.7 safeguards appropriate to sensitivity; organisations must have safeguards and follow proper client-authentication procedures; cases of impostors passing weak authentication.

sources.title: Equipment financing: updating your account information
sources.supports: Lessees contact customer service by phone or e-mail to change address; banking changes need a void cheque from the new account with the lease numbers, sent by fax or e-mail.

sources.title: Equipment financing: lease payments and invoices
sources.supports: Typical lessee questions: payment methods, invoices issued two weeks before due, invoice fee, taxes on payments, past-due interest, payment dates.

sources.title: Equipment financing: end or cancellation of a lease
sources.supports: Leases are non-cancellable; end-of-term options (buy at fair market value or the stated option, renew, return, trade up); letter about 60 days before expiry; customer service arranges returns.

sources.title: Asset-based finance in Canada: the 2019-2020 year (Canadian Market Overview)
sources.supports: March 2020 survey: 40% of respondents had an extreme volume (over 100 a day) of COVID-related calls; deferral requests over half the portfolio for a fifth of respondents; lessees value being able to reach someone to solve an issue and service quality.

sources.title: Rule H1 Pre-Authorized Debits (PADs)
sources.supports: s.15: each debit supported by a payor's PAD agreement; sporadic debits need authorisation each time; one-time debits need a new agreement for later debits. s.30: cancellations honoured in the next cycle.

sources.title: Poll: how many calls do you monitor per agent per month?
sources.supports: 115 respondents: 7% monitor 0-1 calls, 34% 2-4, 26% 5-6, 19% 7-10, 14% 11 or more per agent per month.

assumptions: One case is one contact; the request mix (30% account questions, 13% documents, 12% payouts, 10% changes, 8% disputes, 8% insurance and smaller shares of routed work) is an author estimate.
Hands-on times are set so the average contact takes about 9 minutes of representative time, close to SQM's 589-second handle time; lessor calls are assumed similar to the industry average.

The benchmark median of about 20 minutes is derived from US and North American contact centre data (12 minutes for a call resolved first time), not measured at a Canadian lessor; the simulated median is sensitive to how many contacts are written rather than phoned, because written requests wait hours in the mailbox.
The organisation file lists the operations process and reporting analyst for this process; that work (call statistics and staffing reports) is not per contact and is left out of the steps and FTE.

End-of-term elections are treated as payout or purchase requests to lease administration, because the organisation file has no link from this process to manage-end-of-term; that missing link looks like a gap in the organisation file.
Collections transfers are warm transfers without a business object, as the organisation file has no link from this process to collect-early-stage.
